name: Kulou
description: A star 18 parsecs away, 1.9 times the Sun's width, measured from its light.

radius.source: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 65109: radius 1.872 solar radii, implied by the fitted luminosity 22.456 solar luminosities (fractional uncertainty 0.088) and temperature

temperature.source: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 65109: effective temperature 9191 +/- 421 K, from the fit of a model atmosphere to the star's spectral energy distribution (goodness of fit Q 0.034)

distance.source: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 65109: distance 18.021 pc, the paper's parallax inverted (Gaia DR1's where it revised the star's, else the Hipparcos reduction of van Leeuwen 2007; section 2.3; fractional uncertainty 0.003), at which the luminosity and radius hold

limb.none: no mass is measured and no spectroscopic surface gravity is published with this radius: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770 assume the gravity of their fit (table column 15)

text.card: A star 18 parsecs away, 1.9 times the Sun's width, measured from its light.
text.introduction: Its brightness, measured band by band, gives 22 times the Sun's luminosity at 9,191 K, so 1.872 solar radii.
text.locator: Table 2, HIP 65109: D, Teff, L, Rad, Q

quotes.title: Iota Centauri
quotes.card: Iota Centauri is a star in the southern constellation of Centaurus.
quotes.introduction: It has the proper name Kulou; Iota Centauri is its Bayer designation, which is Latinized from ι Centauri and is abbreviated Iota Cen or ι Cen.

radialVelocity.source: SIMBAD's radial velocity for Gaia DR3 6165699748417797504 (quality A), from 2006AstL...32..759G; Gaia DR3 measures none
